reasons: The lake identity record identifies the case as United States v. Luke Wilson/United States v. Wilson, court 9th Cir., decided 2021-09-21, docket 18-50440.
The lake citation display and official citation are 13 F.4th 961, matching the page citation and 2021 year.
The opinion squarely applies the private-search exception to automated hash matching of Wilson's email attachments.
The opinion expressly discusses contrary Fifth and Sixth Circuit outcomes and says it contributes to growing circuit tension on this issue.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Keep the role tied to private-search/hash-match doctrine, not foreign-search doctrine.

reasons: The court proceeds on the assumption that Wilson had a reasonable expectation of privacy in his email attachments.
The opinion's private-search analysis turns repeatedly on whether Wilson's expectation of privacy was frustrated by Google's earlier conduct.

defect.evidence_quote: We therefore reverse the district court’s denial of Wilson’s motion to suppress and vacate Wilson’s conviction.
defect.problem: The substantive private-search holding is supported, but the final disposition is misstated as Wilson's conviction being reversed. The opinion says the suppression denial was reversed and the conviction was vacated.
defect.proposed_fix: Change the ending to: '... so it was not justified by the private-search exception; the denial of suppression was reversed and Wilson's conviction was vacated.'

reasons: The opinion states that the private-search exception permits repetition only when the government search does not exceed the private search's scope.
The opinion states no Google employee or other person had viewed Wilson's attachments before Agent Thompson did.
The opinion holds Agent Thompson learned new, critical information and expanded the privacy intrusion by opening and viewing the attachments without a warrant.
residual_risks: The lake record has no pinpoints, so support was verified from the cached full opinion text.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Use 'vacated' for the conviction and reserve 'reversed' for the denial of suppression.
